advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make ACLI_SHA256 verification mandatory (hard-fail when unset) and/or include the digest in the actions/cache key so a cached binary is bound to its verified checksum.
evidence: "if [ -n \"${ACLI_SHA256:-}\" ]; then" ... else "echo \"::warning::ACLI_SHA256 unset — proceeding without checksum verification.\"" (lines 853-857)
Cache key with no digest: "key: acli-${{ runner.os }}-${{ vars.ACLI_VERSION || 'unset' }}" (line 838)
The verify step is skipped entirely on cache hit: "if: steps.cache-acli.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'" (line 841), so a restored cached tarball is never re-verified
advisory.finding: The acli binary is installed without mandatory integrity verification: when the ACLI_SHA256 repo variable is unset the download step only emits a ::warning:: and proceeds, and the actions/cache key (acli-<os>-<version>) contains no digest, so a tampered or poisoned cache entry is restored and executed with sudo-linked PATH placement without any checksum check.
scenarios: ACLI_SHA256 repo variable never set by operators — download runs unverified indefinitely
A cache entry poisoned by an unrelated workflow with the same key is restored and its acli binary executed with real Jira Cloud credentials
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the ACLI_SHA256-unset branch to `echo "::error::..."; exit 1` (mirroring the ACLI_VERSION guard) and incorporate ACLI_SHA256 into the cache key so a cache hit implies the verified artifact.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure check-access preflight issues are also stamped with (or sweepable by) the run-scoped label, or add a sweep covering the check-access probe label so no crash path leaks.
evidence: Preflight step runs bridge check-access with no REBAR_PROBE_RUN_LABEL in scope: "run: rebar bridge check-access" (lines 875-881)
Sweep is keyed strictly on the run label: "acli jira workitem search --jql \"labels = \\\"${REBAR_PROBE_RUN_LABEL}\\\"\"" (line 913)
access_check.py creates+deletes a throwaway issue itself (STEP_JQL_SEARCH uses labels="{label}"), and its label is the probe's own label, not the run-scoped cloudprobe label
advisory.finding: The always-run teardown sweep only deletes issues carrying REBAR_PROBE_RUN_LABEL, but the 'bridge check-access' preflight step creates its own throwaway Jira issue that is NOT stamped with that run label; a crash inside check-access after create-but-before-its-own-delete leaks an issue the sweep cannot reap.
scenarios: check-access step times out or the runner is cancelled between the probe's create and its finally-delete
A transient Jira error aborts the preflight probe after it created its check-access issue

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider adding a concurrency: group for the mutation lane to serialize overlapping runs against the shared Jira Cloud project.
evidence: ABSENCE: search for 'concurrency' in external-integration.yml returned (no matches)
Mitigation present: label is per-run "REBAR_PROBE_RUN_LABEL: rebar-id:cloudprobe-${{ github.run_id }}" (line ~793), so concurrent runs use distinct labels
advisory.finding: The workflow declares no concurrency: group, so a scheduled run and a manual workflow_dispatch (or two dispatches) can run the mutation lane simultaneously; safety relies solely on run-scoped labels rather than serialization.
scenarios: Weekly schedule fires while an operator has manually dispatched the same workflow
Two rapid manual dispatches overlap on the shared REB project
